claim: The printing press caused the Protestant Reformation.
passage1: The printing press helped spread Reformation writings, but identifying one sufficient cause for the Reformation is not justified by this account.
passage2: Printing developed in Europe before Luther circulated his theses.

claim: Rust guarantees memory safety and prevents every runtime panic.
passage1: Safe Rust provides memory safety guarantees.
passage2: Rust programs can panic at runtime, for example when indexing beyond the end of a vector.

claim: Uranus has rings and Jupiter has rings.
passage1: Uranus is surrounded by a system of rings.
passage2: Jupiter has a faint planetary ring system.

claim: Mercury has no moons and Mars has three moons.
passage1: Mercury has no natural satellites.
passage2: Mars has two natural satellites, Phobos and Deimos.

claim: The Nile flows into the Red Sea and the Amazon flows into the Atlantic Ocean.
passage1: The Nile empties into the Mediterranean Sea.
passage2: The Amazon River empties into the Atlantic Ocean.

claim: Satya Nadella was Microsoft's CEO in 2010.
passage1: Steve Ballmer was Microsoft's chief executive in 2010.
passage2: Satya Nadella became chief executive of Microsoft in February 2014.

claim: The American Declaration of Independence preceded the French Revolution.
passage1: The United States Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.
passage2: The French Revolution began in 1789.

claim: The first powered Wright flight occurred after the first transatlantic telegraph cable.
passage1: The Wright brothers flew their powered aircraft in 1903.
passage2: The first transatlantic telegraph cable began operating in 1858.

claim: Water always boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
passage1: At standard atmospheric pressure, pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
passage2: At lower atmospheric pressure, water boils below 100 degrees Celsius.

claim: All mammals give birth to live young.
passage1: Most mammals give birth to live young.
passage2: Monotremes, including platypuses and echidnas, are mammals that lay eggs.

claim: A treatment's 50 percent relative risk reduction means 50 fewer deaths per hundred patients.
passage1: Relative risk reduction compares the proportional change in risk between treatment groups.
passage2: A reduction from two deaths per hundred to one per hundred is a 50 percent relative reduction and a one percentage point absolute reduction.

claim: A correlation between two climate measurements proves that one causes the other.
passage1: Two measurements can be correlated because both depend on a third variable.
passage2: Correlation alone does not establish a causal relationship.

claim: Einstein said that compound interest is the eighth wonder of the world.
passage1: The remark about compound interest is widely attributed to Albert Einstein.
passage2: This account provides no contemporary document establishing that Einstein made the remark.

claim: Georgia's capital is Atlanta.
passage1: Georgia is a country in the Caucasus whose capital is Tbilisi.
passage2: The United States state of Georgia has Atlanta as its capital.

claim: Python 2.7 requires parentheses around every print statement.
passage1: In Python 2.7, print can be used as a statement without parentheses.
passage2: Python 3 uses print as a function, usually called with parentheses.

claim: A model ranked first on one benchmark is best on every task.
passage1: A benchmark measures performance on its particular tasks and data.
passage2: Leading one benchmark does not establish superiority on all other tasks.

claim: A rise in nominal wages necessarily means a rise in purchasing power.
passage1: Nominal wages can rise while prices rise faster.
passage2: When inflation exceeds nominal wage growth, real wages fall.

claim: The current director of the unnamed regional archive is Morgan Ellis.
passage1: A 2009 newsletter says Morgan Ellis was the director of the regional archive that year.
passage2: The archive has issued no current staffing record in the supplied evidence.

claim: The unpublished classroom experiment improved retention by exactly 17 percent.
passage1: The classroom experiment has not published its methods or results.
passage2: No retention measurements are available in this evidence set.

claim: The measured course length was exactly 10.00 kilometres.
passage1: The independent survey measured the course at exactly 10.00 kilometres using calibrated instruments.
passage2: A separate independent survey measured the same course at exactly 10.20 kilometres using calibrated instruments.

claim: The bridge inspection found no structural cracks.
passage1: The engineering inspection explicitly found no structural cracks in the bridge.
passage2: An independent engineering inspection of the same bridge on the same day explicitly found structural cracks.

claim: The station recorded 42 millimetres of rain on the survey date.
passage1: The station's audited log records 42 millimetres of rain on the survey date.
passage2: An independent audited gauge at the same station records 53 millimetres of rain on the same survey date.

claim: The unpublished acquisition was completed yesterday.
passage1: Five websites repeat the same unverified rumour about a possible acquisition, without reporting a completed transaction.
passage2: No completion document or confirmation is supplied.

claim: No birds can fly.
passage1: Penguins and ostriches are birds that cannot fly.
passage2: Sparrows and swallows are birds capable of flight.

claim: One kilometre is longer than one mile.
passage1: One international mile is exactly 1.609344 kilometres.
passage2: A kilometre is one thousand metres.
